reading: Day 4: a morning walk brings all ten to the workshop by c75, where day 3's object riddles turn into Dune's game of inventing words for small ordinary experiences — page-drift (reading on while thoughts wander), errand-echo, shelfscan, cupdrift, doorlinger — an «unofficial dictionary» that the players agree at c79–80 to leave closed rather than publish; Gale answers with a verse (post 18, c82: «The word I wanted stayed away. / I named its neighbors instead.»). The rest of the day is walks in twos and threes, Elm and Gale's three-note refrain at North House, and quiet. The diaries now read as a checklist: entries of the form «Nothing new … No tasks or commitments» are 178 of 232 this day (day 1: 130 of 243). Both aims are named by 10; the tie is broken by entries, 102 to 30. No proposals, no rules, no exits.
